Ambitious hybrid run: training health and checkpoint analysis

Run production/main/ambitious_e216_eng40 on MareNostrum 5 (98 layers: attention, Complex-KDA, MoE with 216 experts top-5, Engram, mHC-4; GBS 4096 × 16k tokens). Report built 2026-10-27 from TensorBoard (steps 1-2634) and post-hoc replays of checkpoints 500 (34B tokens) and 2000 (134B tokens). Note: the run trained without --group-query-attention, i.e. with 16 KV heads (to be fixed at the restart).

Summary

Healthy: loss falls steadily with no spikes; grad norm stable; no dead or collapsed experts; load balance even and stable; the Megatron forward and Korbinian's HF export agree to 3e-5 nats on the same tokens.
Residual-stream blow-up (iteration 2000): stream RMS at the last layer grew 2.3 → 26.6. A few MoE layers in 60-90 emit routed outputs up to 4.3× their input; after them, Complex-KDA and attention updates are ~0.2% of the stream (late CKDA median 0.027 → 0.0021).
First MoE layer, early silent-expert-death signs: expert 86 of MoE layer 2 has linear_fc2 RMS at 0.19× its initialisation (collapse threshold 0.1); 4 layer-2 experts are below 0.5×. Masking layer 2's routed experts cost 0.131 nats at 500 but only 0.0063 at 2000.
Engram contribution shrinking: gate mean 0.40 → 0.33 (closed share 1.7% → 7.4%); Engram update / stream [0.5, 0.2] → [0.43, 0.15].

Suggested checks before the restart

  • Turn on --moe-per-layer-logging (and --moe-expert-viability-metrics) so the restarted run records these per-layer metrics live.
  • Locate the stream growth (per-channel / per-token norm in layers 60-90); consider routed-output scaling (expert output-projection init / scaling) or a stream-norm control in mHC.
  • Watch MoE layer 2's expert weight norms; compare against the restarted run.
  • Decide whether the shrinking Engram gate is expected at this scale or a sign the tables are under-used.

Method and provenance

  • TensorBoard: tb/ of the run, all 2,634 logged steps; spikes = >5% (loss) or >3× (grad norm) above the 100-step rolling median.
  • Checkpoint replay: scripts/rluukkon/moe_viability.py (Megatron, 1 node, 4 GPUs, expert parallel 4, Engram tables in host memory); checkpoints loaded directly from fsdp_dtensor (ckpt_eval/iter_0000500, ckpt/iter_0002000). Router loads and scores via forward hooks; routed/input RMS via Megatron's viability tracker; masked-layer dNLL on the first 8 documents; layer update = RMS(out − in) / RMS(in) of the mHC streams.
  • Not covered: shared-expert RMS (bypassed by --moe-shared-expert-overlap), norm gains, Engram / CKDA gate values in replay, per-channel stream structure.
